dimensions.evidence: Input f in Hz (T^-1), output T in s (T). Expression 1/T^-1=T is coherent; Hz and s both unit scale, no MHz division inlined. Period is elapsed time per complete cycle, not any generic duration.

guards-inverses.evidence: Guard f>0 rejects the f=0 domain case (no finite period) and the missing-input case, both present. Inverse f=1/T has one positive root for T>0; recomputed 1/2.5=0.4 and 1/4e-7=2.5e6. T=0 is undefined and f=0 admits no finite T, both correctly excluded. No sign branches.

reference-independence.evidence: All three references recomputed. published-string-period: 1/2=0.5 vs expected 0.5, tol 0.005 is half the 0.01 s reporting step. independent-cycle-count: ten equally timed cycles spanning 25 s gives 25/10=2.5 s per cycle with f=10/25=0.4 Hz, an independent counting route vs expected 2.5. published-ultrasound: 1/2.5e6=4e-7 vs 4e-7, tol 5e-10 is half the 0.001 us reporting increment. Published nominal values preserved as expected, not replaced by recomputation.

Explicitly NOT new scientific coverage: duplicate_of computer-science--clock-cycle-time@r1 is set, and the record's own summary restricts it to overlap-evidence/metadata correction. source-fidelity.evidence: Live-inspected UP1 Sec 15.1: Eq 15.1 f=1/T with period defined as time for one complete oscillation and frequency as oscillations per unit time; Example 15.1 pairs 0.400 us with 2.50e6 Hz. Live-inspected UP1 Sec 16.1: wave period/frequency with f=1/T and Example 16.1(b) T=1/2.00=0.50 s. T=1/f serialization preserves the canonical relation; the numerator 1 is the dimensionless count of one complete cycle. Overlap claim confirmed by direct inspection: the UVM clock-cycle-time bullet states it is the reciprocal of clock frequency, and the UMN Clock Time section states clock time is the clock period and the reciprocal of clock frequency. Same full-cycle reciprocal definition under different contexts.

sources.finding: Paraphrased: period T is the time to complete one oscillation; frequency f is oscillations per unit time; f=1/T (Eq 15.1); 1 Hz is one cycle per second. Example 15.1: 0.400 us period gives 2.50e6 Hz ultrasound. Footer: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, LLM/AI prior-permission assertion, Rice copyright.
sources.locator: Sec 15.1 Period and Frequency in Oscillations, Eq 15.1; Example 15.1.

sources.finding: Paraphrased: wave period T is the time for one complete oscillation; frequency f=1/T; period usually in seconds, frequency in Hz. Example 16.1(b): period is the inverse of the 2.00 Hz drive, T=1/2.00=0.50 s.

Paraphrased: clock cycle time is the duration of a single cycle and is the reciprocal of clock frequency (2 GHz gives 0.500 ns, 3 GHz about 0.333 ns). Page credit: adapted from Patterson and Hennessy by Malik and Cafiero; published 2026-10-05; no reuse license stated.
